newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine reserves double to $4 bln in 1996-c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine reserves double to $4 bln in 1996-c.bank.

text.p: Ukraine's hard currency reserves doubled to $4 billion at the end of last year from $2 billion at the start, central bank chief Viktor Yushchenko told parliament on Friday.
"The national bank's hard currency reserves almost doubled and at the end of the year had reached $4 billion while 18 months ago they were valued at $2 billion," Yushchenko said.
Increasing volumes on the currency market showed the stability of the national hryvnia unit, which was introduced in September 1996 at 1.76 to the dollar and opened at 1.8590 on Thursday, he said.
In May turnover on the currency market stood at $2.6 billion, up from $1.5 billion in the same month last year and $535 million in May 1995, Yushchenko said.
The hryvnia lost 5.5 percent of its value in 1996 after a 72.3 percent decline the previous year, he added.
